newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold catches Indian festival demand.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold catches Indian festival demand.

text.p: Indian demand for gold from the Gulf trading post of Dubai is picking up ahead of India's festival and wedding season, Dubai traders said on Sunday.

Local and re-export turnover in Dubai bullion and jewellery markets was steadily increasing ahead the Hindu festival of Diwali in November and the second Indian marriage season running from November to April.
Both events are traditionally celebrated with purchases of gold -- bought from proceeds of the harvest -- to an extent that makes India the world's largest consumer of the metal.
"Indian goldsmiths and jewellers are buying ahead to meet the demand. The Indian harvest has been a good one this year," a Dubai trader said.
With the end of the monsoon rains farmers in India are beginning to deliver the first cash crops of the country's winter harvest, Dubai shopowners in the gold souk said.
Dubai gold sellers' hopes of strong gold sales have been raised by forecasts of a robust harvest. Indian rice output is expected to reach 75 tonnes, up from nearly 71 tonnes last year.
The prospect of strong India demand comes as a relief for many traders in Dubai after the decline in turnover during the hot Gulf summer when customers leave for cooler climes.
"The market is improving...demand is on an upswing because of festival demand and lower prices," an Indian expatriate gold trader based in Dubai said.
Dubai is the main source of gold to India through official sales and smuggling by the large expatriate communities working in the oil-rich United Arab Emirates (UAE).
The emergence of bullion buying has also been helped by lower gold prices, traders said.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola bar (TT) -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was quoted by Dubai traders on Sunday at 5,260 UAE dirhams ($1,433.25), down seven dirhams on the week.
TT bars in Bombay were quoted by Dubai traders at $1,672, an attractive 16-17 percent arbitrage trading window.
Ten gram pieces in Dubai were quoted at 449 dirhams.
International spot bullion was last quoted on Sunday at $380.40-90 an ounce, hovering above key $380 support but well adrift from the six-year high of $414.80 hit on February 5.
Silver in Dubai was quoted at $159.79 a kilo.
